acceptance_criteria.requirement: No large selected-date details panel in any dashboard or preview composition.
No due-deck list or separate selected-date events column on the dashboard.
No dashboard Most Missed preview list.
Month and Year end with one integrated CalendarFooter surface containing the legend and context; it is not a nested floating card.

The footer legend exposes three immediately distinguishable groups: Completion with exact heat-scale samples, Reviews due samples with the same soft backgrounds and bottom markers as cells, and the surface-haloed Event diamond.
The selected-date line uses an accent Today chip or neutral Selected chip followed by one nonduplicated short date.
The global next-event row reads NEXT EVENT, gives the title more weight than metadata, uses weekday/date plus an in N days countdown, and never uses +N days.
The unmistakable pencil edit control sits directly after event metadata and opens that event; No upcoming event hides the marker and edit control.

Reviewed-card and due-card actions use the solid primary accent treatment at 30 pixels, use date-appropriate labels, and are hidden rather than disabled when no exact card set exists; Most missed remains conditional and secondary.
Historical tooltips use Completed reviews and New cards studied; future tooltips use Reviews due and New cards due only when supported.

Future reviews due use one of five explicit low-chroma violet backgrounds plus one of five stronger violet bottom markers; saturated full-cell purple is prohibited and future dates with zero reviews remain neutral.
Cell layers remain composable in this order: base classification, completion or Reviews Due visualization, out-of-month treatment, Today, Event, hover, Selected, and keyboard focus.

Reviews Due marker height is stable across intensity: Month uses a one-pixel inset band clamped from two to four pixels and Year uses at least two pixels or roughly 34 percent of its compact cell height; only the five marker colors encode intensity.
Due-load normalization uses one robust p90 reference so a single outlier cannot flatten the forecast.
At 940 pixels and wider, Month and Year use the same calendar-left and insight-rail-right shell with stable column widths.
From 440 to 939 pixels the two-by-two metric grid sits below the calendar; only widths below 440 pixels use one card per row.

Year preserves the responsive 53-column square-cell grid, occupies roughly 90 to 94 percent of the supported calendar body up to its readable maximum, centers vertically, and shows stronger month labels without clipping.
The persistent insight rail orders Today’s Progress, Today’s Session, Last 7 Days, and All Time, then the Bible verse; switching views changes only the calendar body.
The four statistics cards remain a two-by-two rail at established widths, use a stable label/value grid, 5.5 to 6 pixel row rhythm, and readable 9.5 to 11.5 pixel small text.

Today’s Progress is a six-pixel contiguous Completed, New, Learning, and Reviews workload bar on a muted track; widths derive from displayed counts, Buried stays outside the denominator, and zero totals create no sliver or invalid width.

New, Learning, Reviews, Buried, and New cards studied keep stable semantic colors; Retention and Again rate are independently target-aware for success, warning, and danger, while untargeted and lifetime metrics remain neutral.

Every light mode paints the full viewport with a tinted canvas behind white main cards; neutral borders and small neutral shadows separate cards without colored glow or dependence on external screenshot framing.

Dark modes use primarily neutral canvas, card, control, border, and heading layers; theme chroma is concentrated in active controls, primary actions, completion data, and small accents rather than every surface.
The Bible verse remains last in the insight rail, uses a larger untruncated quote, a legible secondary reference in every dark theme, and reduced unused vertical space.

Month and Year, previous, Today, next, and settings controls share a 29 to 30 pixel height; active segments use accent-soft fill, accent text, and accent-border without glow; compact headers retain two rows.
Month and Year share delegated selection and state overlays; view switching preserves the selected date and does not remount the insight rail.
The layout refactor changes no study definition, saved preference, event, verse, statistics source, or removed-component schema slot.

Wide footers keep the solid primary action aligned across both context rows; compact footers stack date, event, and the 30 to 32 pixel full-width action while very narrow layouts use nine-pixel side padding and no page-level horizontal overflow.
Every theme and mode exposes the complete neutral, accent, semantic, heat, calendar-state, disabled, shadow, and overlay token contract.

Sapphire Glass remains the default, uses a lightly tinted canvas and optional restrained top-level card gradient, keeps dark surfaces neutral navy-charcoal, and reserves stronger blue for interaction and completion.
Graphite stays cool-neutral, uses blue only for focus and selection visibility, caps dark completion at medium-light steel, and keeps the completed progress segment darker than the primary button.

High Contrast uses black only on the outer dark canvas, near-black elevated cards, stronger luminance steps, state-proportional boundaries, controlled teal completion, desaturated due colors, and no ambient shadow or neon treatment.

Emerald dark uses almost-neutral charcoal canvas and cards, reserves green for active controls, primary action, completion, progress, and selection, and keeps cyan, orange, violet, slate, and gold semantics stable.
New, Learning, Review, Buried, Success, Warning, Danger, and Event palettes remain identical across themes within each color mode.

Month and Year completion cells share one explicit opaque six-level theme scale while Reviews Due uses the same stable five-level background and marker tokens in every theme; only marker thickness adapts to cell size.

Completion date text is explicitly mapped by level: light 0 through 3 use primary and 4 through 5 use white; dark 0 through 3 use primary and 4 through 5 use #0B1116; due dates use primary and outside dates remain muted.

Today preserves the data fill under a two-pixel inset theme-accent ring, Selected uses a surface-haloed focus ring, and combined Today plus Selected exposes both layers without violet or blurred glow.

Event diamonds use the stable gold token plus a one-pixel surface halo, stay upper-right at Month and Year sizes, and remain visible over every completion and Reviews Due level without tinting the full cell.
Month preserves 34 to 40 pixel cells, 10 pixel minimum date text, five-to-six-pixel internal spacing, stronger weekday labels, and nearly neutral adjacent-month dates without full completion color.

Dashboard controls, settings previews, tooltips, warnings, scrollbars, empty states, and native settings chrome consume semantic tokens or the native application palette without stale component colors.
The production hardcoded-color audit reports no unexplained component-level color literals and SVG icons inherit currentColor wherever practical.

The exact packaged add-on must pass source/archive parity, the 96-case automated matrix, eight 100-percent complete color-state fixtures, all 32 native theme/mode/view/layout captures, full-screen viewport checks, the contrast report, and the classified hardcoded-color audit; human and cross-platform gates remain separate.
